sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.

body.tldr: The paper constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest pointwise CATE interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the uniform-design attainable submodel.  Projected private spline pilots, a clipped higher-order local moment, joint Gaussian releases, and spectral stabilization yield the achieved phase-sensitive length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) there; this is not transferred to the full class.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), a separate all-observation, fixed-dimensional private direct-regression interval is honest and has the nonsharp \(\beta\)-smooth upper \(1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}\).  Together with the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower bound, this replaces the trivial length-two endpoint by a nontrivial full-class bracket while leaving the exact private confidence modulus open.

project_justification.gap: Private CATE papers provide point releases or quasi-oracle guarantees, and private causal interval papers treat regular average effects. They do not give a uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage theorem that accounts simultaneously for higher-order nuisance bias, sampling uncertainty, privacy composition, and privacy noise.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on a fixed KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference without assuming the desired coverage or length and without relying on the rejected paired-microcell lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment for the attainable higher-order construction, proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, uniform finite-sample coverage, and the phase-sensitive mean interval length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Separately, it proves both an ordinary regression lower limitation and an explicit fixed-dimensional direct-regression upper on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the full-class bracket is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\).  The attainable higher-order upper is not transferred to the full class, and exact sharpness remains unresolved.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed higher-order identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  The new full-class result instead uses standard fixed-dimensional direct regression: overlap and the local density band condition the two population Grams, while armwise \(\beta\)-smooth Taylor bias yields a deliberately nonsharp private upper.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the attainable quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present intervals use explicit uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism and post-processing fact used by both private constructions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\) of the clipped quadratic-moment release and is proved only as an attainable-submodel upper cost.  The separate full-class direct-regression release has sensitivity \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\) but incurs armwise bias \(O(h^\beta)\), so it does not determine whether the smoother \(\gamma\)-contrast, the nuisance interaction \(q\), or a stabilized private Gram controls the sharp frontier.  The invalid paired-microcell transport step is not revived.
body.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), its achieved length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, the ordinary full-class lower limitation, and the new fixed-dimensional direct-regression coverage and upper bound on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  The attainable class is restricted to uniform design; its higher-order upper is not transferred to the full class.  Under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the settled full-class result is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\).  Whether this bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains the open-ended question.
